name: CyberArena 3D
pitchShort: A neon first-person arena shooter that runs in your browser. Pick a callsign and armor colour, then fight AI practice bots with a live scoreboard and kill feed. Free, no install.
descriptionLong:
CyberArena 3D is a free first-person shooter built with Three.js that runs right in the browser, with no download or account.

Choose a callsign and an armor colour, deploy into a neon cyber arena and fight three AI practice bots. Move with W, A, S, D, aim with the mouse, click to fire your laser rifle and press Space to jump. On phones and tablets there is an on-screen joystick, a look area, and fire and jump buttons.

The HUD shows your health, kills, deaths and streak, plus a live scoreboard and kill feed. When you are eliminated you respawn after a short countdown.

CyberArena is in testing / development. Right now it runs in single-player Local Arena mode against bots; online multiplayer is planned but not switched on yet.

name: Stack Attack Arena
pitchShort: 1v1 neon falling-block combat. Clear lines to send garbage into your rival's well. Quick Match online, vs bot or endless. Free in your browser.
descriptionLong:
Stack Attack Arena is a free 1v1 falling-block battle game that runs in your browser on phone or desktop.

Clear two or more lines to send garbage into your rival's well, and top out and you lose. Tap Quick Match to be paired online in seconds, or play a friend with a 4-letter room code or share link. You can also take on the bot (Easy, Normal or Hard) or chase a global high score in Endless.

It has hold, ghost piece, a 7-bag, combos and garbage cancelling. Phones get touch buttons and swipe controls, and desktop uses the keyboard. There's no download or sign-up.

© 2026 Kerzy Labs

name: Quad Pong
pitchShort: 4-player neon free-for-all Pong. Defend your wall, and the last wall standing wins. Quick Match online or solo against 3 bots.
descriptionLong:
Quad Pong is a free four-player Pong game that runs in your browser.

Each player defends one wall. Miss the ball and you lose a life, and once you're out your wall turns solid. Tap Quick Match to fill a room automatically, with bots taking any empty seats, or host a room and send friends a 4-letter code or link. Solo mode puts you against three bots with a choice of difficulty and lives.

Extra balls and speed-ups keep rounds short. On phones you drag, and on desktop you use the mouse or keys.

© 2026 Kerzy Labs

name: Rival Lanes
pitchShort: A neon tower defense game in your browser. Pick a class, place towers anywhere off the path, and hold back the waves in Classic, Endless or live PvP. Free, no install.
descriptionLong:
Rival Lanes is a free tower defense game that runs in your browser, on phones and desktop.

Choose a class and a starter tower, then place towers freely on the grid and upgrade them as the waves grow. Play Classic or Endless and post your score to the global leaderboard, or go head to head in PvP by room code, quick match or against a bot, sending attackers into your rival's lane.

It's still in testing, so there's a Feedback button in the menu for feature requests and bug reports.

© 2026 Kerzy Labs

name: Ollama
pitchShort: Run open large language models such as Llama, Gemma, Qwen and DeepSeek on your own Mac, Windows or Linux machine with one command.
descriptionLong:
Ollama is a free, open-source (MIT) tool for running large language models locally. Pull a model with one command and chat with it in the terminal, or call it from your own apps through a local REST API that is also compatible with the OpenAI API format.

It runs on macOS, Windows and Linux, uses your GPU when available, and keeps your prompts on your own machine. A large library of open models is available, and you can build custom models with a Modelfile.

Source code: https://github.com/ollama/ollama

name: Open WebUI
pitchShort: A self-hosted, ChatGPT-style web interface for local and cloud AI models, with chat history, document RAG, users and plugins.
descriptionLong:
Open WebUI is a feature-rich, self-hosted AI chat interface that works offline. Connect it to Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible API and get a polished web app with conversations, model switching, document upload and retrieval (RAG), web search, multi-user accounts with roles, and an extension system for tools and functions.

It installs with Docker or pip. The source is on GitHub (https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui) under the Open WebUI License, a BSD-3-based licence that adds a branding-preservation clause for larger deployments; check it if you plan to rebrand.

Free to self-host.

name: Excalidraw
pitchShort: A virtual whiteboard for sketching hand-drawn-style diagrams, wireframes and flowcharts, with live collaboration and end-to-end encryption.
descriptionLong:
Excalidraw is a free, open-source (MIT) virtual whiteboard. It gives diagrams and wireframes a friendly hand-drawn look, works in the browser with no sign-up, and supports real-time collaboration with end-to-end encrypted sharing links.

Drawings can be exported to PNG, SVG or the open .excalidraw format, and developers can embed the editor in their own apps with the @excalidraw/excalidraw React package. A paid Excalidraw+ plan exists for teams, but the editor itself is free and open source.

Source code: https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw

name: n8n
pitchShort: A visual workflow automation tool with 400+ integrations and AI agent nodes. Fair-code: free to self-host, source-available under the Sustainable Use License.
descriptionLong:
n8n lets you build automations by connecting nodes on a canvas: triggers, hundreds of app integrations, code steps in JavaScript or Python, and AI nodes for building LLM agents and RAG pipelines.

About the licence, honestly: n8n is fair-code, not OSI open source. The source is public on GitHub (https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n) under the Sustainable Use License, which lets you self-host and use it for free for your own internal business purposes, but restricts reselling it as a hosted service. Some enterprise features use a separate licence, and n8n also sells a paid cloud plan.

The self-hosted Community Edition is free.

name: Godot Engine
pitchShort: A free, MIT-licensed 2D and 3D game engine with its own editor, GDScript and C# support, and exports to desktop, mobile and the web.
descriptionLong:
Godot is a complete, cross-platform game engine for 2D and 3D games. It ships as a small download with a full editor, a scene and node system, the Python-like GDScript language plus C# and C++ (GDExtension) support, physics, animation, UI and shader tools.

Games can be exported to Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS and the web. Godot is released under the MIT licence with no royalties or fees, and is developed by a community supported by the non-profit Godot Foundation.

Source code: https://github.com/godotengine/godot

name: Blender
pitchShort: The free, open-source 3D creation suite: modelling, sculpting, animation, rendering, compositing, video editing and 2D animation in one app.
descriptionLong:
Blender covers the whole 3D pipeline: modelling, sculpting, UV and texturing, rigging and animation, simulation, the Cycles and EEVEE renderers, compositing, motion tracking, video editing and Grease Pencil 2D animation.

It runs on Windows, macOS and Linux, is scriptable with Python, and is released under the GNU GPL. Development is led by the Blender Foundation and Blender Institute and funded by the community through the Blender Development Fund.

Source code: https://projects.blender.org/blender/blender

name: Coolify
pitchShort: An open-source, self-hostable alternative to Heroku, Netlify and Vercel: deploy apps, databases and 280+ one-click services to your own servers.
descriptionLong:
Coolify turns your own VPS or bare-metal servers into a platform-as-a-service. Connect a Git repository and it builds and deploys your app (Dockerfile, Nixpacks or Docker Compose), with automatic SSL, preview deployments, databases with backups, and a catalogue of one-click services.

Coolify is open source under the Apache 2.0 licence and free to self-host on as many servers as you like, with no vendor lock-in. A paid Coolify Cloud plan is available if you would rather not host the dashboard yourself.

Source code: https://github.com/coollabsio/coolify

name: VSCodium
pitchShort: Free, community-built binaries of Microsoft's VS Code source, MIT-licensed and without Microsoft's telemetry or branding.
descriptionLong:
VSCodium builds the open-source VS Code codebase into ready-to-install releases for Windows, macOS and Linux. You get the same editor, minus Microsoft telemetry and proprietary branding. Extensions come from the Open VSX registry.

Source code: https://github.com/VSCodium/vscodium

name: Supabase
pitchShort: An open-source Firebase alternative built on Postgres: database, auth, storage, realtime and edge functions. Self-host it or use the hosted free tier.
descriptionLong:
Supabase gives every project a full Postgres database plus auth, file storage, realtime subscriptions, edge functions and auto-generated APIs. The whole stack is open source and can be self-hosted with Docker. The hosted service has a free tier.

Source code: https://github.com/supabase/supabase

name: Penpot
pitchShort: Open-source design and prototyping tool for designers and developers, built on open web standards (SVG, CSS). Runs in the browser or self-hosted.
descriptionLong:
Penpot is a browser-based design and prototyping tool, similar in spirit to Figma, that stores designs as open standards like SVG and CSS. It has components, flex and grid layouts, design tokens, code inspect and real-time collaboration. Use the free cloud or self-host it.

Source code: https://github.com/penpot/penpot

name: Plausible Analytics
pitchShort: Lightweight, cookie-free, privacy-friendly web analytics. The Community Edition is open source and free to self-host.
descriptionLong:
Plausible is a simple, privacy-focused alternative to Google Analytics. The script is under 1 KB, it uses no cookies and collects no personal data. Plausible Community Edition (AGPL) is free to self-host; the hosted cloud version is paid.

Source code: https://github.com/plausible/analytics

name: Immich
pitchShort: Self-hosted photo and video backup with mobile apps, face recognition, maps and smart search. An open-source Google Photos alternative.
descriptionLong:
Immich backs up photos and videos from your phone to your own server. It has iOS and Android apps, a web interface, albums and sharing, face recognition, a map view and machine-learning search, all running on hardware you control.

Source code: https://github.com/immich-app/immich

name: Jan
pitchShort: An open-source desktop app for chatting with AI models that run fully offline on your computer, with optional cloud model connections.
descriptionLong:
Jan is a ChatGPT-style desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux that downloads and runs open models locally, so your chats stay on your machine. It also exposes a local OpenAI-compatible API server and can connect to cloud providers if you want.

Source code: https://github.com/janhq/jan

name: ComfyUI
pitchShort: A powerful node-based interface for image, video and audio generation with open models like Stable Diffusion and Flux, run locally on your GPU.
descriptionLong:
ComfyUI lets you build generative AI pipelines by wiring nodes together in a graph. It supports a wide range of open image, video and audio models, runs on your own hardware, and has a large community library of custom nodes and shareable workflows.

Source code: https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI

name: OBS Studio
pitchShort: Free, open-source software for screen recording and live streaming, with scenes, sources, audio mixing and plugins.
descriptionLong:
OBS Studio records and streams video on Windows, macOS and Linux. Build scenes from screens, windows, webcams and media, mix audio with filters, and stream to Twitch, YouTube and others. Great for devlogs, demos and tutorials.

Source code: https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio

name: Audacity
pitchShort: The free, open-source audio editor and recorder for cleaning up voice-overs, podcasts, sound effects and music.
descriptionLong:
Audacity is a multi-track audio editor and recorder for Windows, macOS and Linux. Record, cut, mix and apply effects like noise reduction, compression and EQ. Useful for game sound effects, trailers and podcast audio.

Source code: https://github.com/audacity/audacity

name: Bruno
pitchShort: An open-source, offline-first API client. Collections are plain-text files you keep in your Git repo, with no cloud account required.
descriptionLong:
Bruno is a fast desktop API client, an alternative to Postman and Insomnia. It stores collections as plain-text .bru files on your disk, so you can version and review them in Git alongside your code. It works offline with no forced sign-in.

Source code: https://github.com/usebruno/bruno

name: Hoppscotch
pitchShort: A lightweight, open-source API development ecosystem in your browser: REST, GraphQL, WebSocket and more, with a self-hostable server.
descriptionLong:
Hoppscotch is a fast, browser-based API client for REST, GraphQL, WebSocket, SSE, MQTT and Socket.IO. It has collections, environments and team workspaces, plus desktop apps and a self-hostable Community Edition.

Source code: https://github.com/hoppscotch/hoppscotch

name: Airhand
pitchShort: Control live radio, your own music and a timer with hand gestures in front of your camera. Swipe to change station or song, pinch to play, circle for volume. Early Access, coming soon.
descriptionLong:
Airhand turns the camera on your phone, tablet or computer into a hands-free remote for live radio, your own music and a timer.

The gestures (v1.2):
- Swipe left or right: previous or next station or song.
- Swipe up or down: move up or down the list. On the timer, add or remove a minute.
- Pinch your thumb and index finger, or touch your thumb to your middle finger as if to snap: play, pause or start.
- Draw a circle with one finger: volume. Clockwise is louder, counter-clockwise is quieter. It takes about two thirds of a turn before the first step, so small wobbles don't change it.
- Optional: hold an open palm to stop (on by default) and hold a fist to mute (off by default, experimental). Both can be switched in Settings.

After a swipe, Airhand ignores the hand moving back, both up/down and left/right, and waits until your hand is still or out of view. You can change that pause and how big a swipe must be in Settings. A short practice checklist helps you try each gesture once, and every gesture shows what it did on screen.

Radio has live stations from Canada and 20 other countries; if one can't play, Airhand offers the next. My Music plays songs from your device, and they stay on your device. Timer has a countdown and a stopwatch.

Hand tracking runs on your device. The camera picture is never recorded or uploaded. Every gesture also has a tap button and a keyboard key.

Honest notes: Airhand is in testing (Early Access). The gestures are tested with recorded hand paths and need more real-webcam testing, and lighting and camera angle matter. The "snap" is read from the camera as the thumb touching the middle finger; there is no sound detection. Airhand is not on sale yet; it is coming soon at $6.99, with future updates included.
